subject: Greenroom logistics, secure breakout feeds and sim-bridge plan for July exec workshop
messages:
From: Ryan Bishop <ryan@studioav.com>

Cc: 
Date: 2026-06-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial greenroom/secure-feed options for Acme exec workshop (level 4)

Hi Hannah / Marissa,

Following our site visit this morning at Acme (level 4 — west tower), I sketched two greenroom/secure-feed options that will handle simultaneous executive breakouts and a simulated external feed for the investor panel:

- Option A: Two adjacent secure greenrooms (locked, KMS-backed recorder) with dedicated 1Gbps VLANs, AES-256 SRT for offsite feed.
- Option B: Single large greenroom with partitioned ISO booths, redundant encoders, and per-breakout SRTP substreams.

Key constraints we noticed: limited cat6 drops in the greenroom corridor, a single redundant upstream fiber path through the service shaft, and building security requires vendor staff visitor passes by 10:30am day-of.

I've attached a preliminary floor sketch and the mic rider (input list). Can you confirm your preference and whether Redwood wants vendor-managed recorders (StudioAV) or for you to supply a locked HSM-managed recorder?

Attachments: studioav_greenroom_plan_v1.pdf, mic_rider_and-input_list.xlsx

Happy to hop on a quick call to talk failover and encryption specifics.

- Ryan

Subject: Re: Initial greenroom/secure-feed options for Acme exec workshop (level 4)

Thanks Ryan — good notes and thanks for the quick sketch. Three clarifications from our side:

1) Recorder ownership: Redwood will supply the HSM/KMS-wrapped recorder for compliance reasons. StudioAV should provide encoder/transcoder and manage live routing, but all final master recordings must be deposited to our recorder over an encrypted SFTP after each session.

2) Secure breakout feeds: We prefer Option A for isolation (two locked greenrooms). Each room needs an independent PTS-validated stream with per-stream audit logs. Can StudioAV supply per-stream audit headers forwarded to a syslog endpoint (we'll provide host/port)?

3) Bandwidth and fallback: The west tower fiber is fine but we need a documented fallback — can you propose on-site 5G backup (bonded) and a warm standby encoder in a separate physical rack?

Action items:
- Ryan: update plan to Option A with KMS recorder handoff steps and per-stream audit header support.
- Marissa: confirm vendor pass process with Acme security and share contact.
- Karthik: can you review required network ACLs and confirm whether we need a VPC peering arrangement or a temporary VLAN in Acme's tenant?

I can be on a 30-min call Thursday 6/26 at 11:00am PT if that helps.

Thanks,
Hannah

On Thu, Jun 24, 2026 at 2:40 PM Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Ryan — good notes and thanks for the quick sketch. Three clarifications from our side:

Hi all — updated plan attached. Summary of changes:

- Switched to Option A: two locked greenrooms (G1 / G2) with separate 1Gbps VLANs, physical lockboxes for HSM recorder handoff.
- Per-stream audit: encoders will emit RFC5424-format audit headers pushed to your syslog endpoint over TLS (please provide FQDN and port). We can also mirror headers to a separate S3 bucket for retention.
- Fallbacks: on-site bonded 5G (2 SIMs / carrier diversity) will be staged, plus a warm standby encoder in the adjacent comms closet (physically isolated rack).
- Cabling: we propose using an IP67-rated patch path to avoid corridor traffic during load-in; we'll bring 4 temporary Cat6 runs and a secondary fiber mux.

Attachments: studioav_greenroom_plan_v2.pdf (updated wiring and rack layout), mic_rider_and-input_list.xlsx, acme_floorplan_level4.png

Open Qs for Acme/Redwood:
- HSM handoff window: how many minutes can the recorder be offline during swap?
- On-site credentials: final list of vendor staff who need permanent access passes.

Elena — looping you here to confirm building pass flow and whether Acme can provision vendor badges the morning of the event (we need badges by 8:30am day-of).

Best,
Ryan

Subject: Final confirmation — greenroom ops, vendor list and day-of windows (ACME week of 7/19)

Elena / Ryan — final confirmations before we lock the run sheet.

Confirmed items:
- Redwood will bring the HSM-wrapped master recorder and will perform a hot-swap handoff between sessions. Recorder offline window: maximum 90 seconds during seed-to-master copy; StudioAV please plan a rolling short-term buffer to avoid dropped frames.
- StudioAV: per-stream audit headers will be shipped to syslog.redwood-internal.example.com:6514 over TLS. We will provide a signed cert for mutual TLS next week.
- Vendor passes: Acme will issue day-of badges at the concierge for the following staff: Ryan Bishop, Marta Silva, Daniel Cho (StudioAV). Badges available at 8:00am 7/20.
- Backup: bonded 5G will be live and tested during tech rehearsal on 7/20 at 09:00am. Warm standby encoder racked 2N away from main encoder.

Open items before Friday 7/16:
- Marissa: confirm final list of StudioAV staff for building passes and share photo IDs.
- Karthik: provide the minimal ACL change list for Acme IT to allow the VLAN peering (we need those rules in Acme's change window 7/18 02:00-04:00).
- Ryan: upload studioav_greenroom_plan_v2.pdf to the shared Drive and confirm estimated load-in time (we requested 3 hours but can compress to 2:15 with extra crew).

If there are no blockers I will publish the run sheet and add the vendor contact numbers. Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround — see you at rehearsal.
